detailed_description: The Date Calculator precisely performs date arithmetic by accounting for time zones, leap years, and calendar irregularities. It employs the ISO 8601 standard for date parsing and utilizes JavaScript's Date object to handle complex operations like adding milliseconds across Daylight Saving Time (DST) transitions. Developers can calculate differences in days, weeks, months, or years between two dates, or adjust a start date by a specified duration. This tool is essential for project planning requiring precise deadline tracking, financial calculations involving compounding periods, or historical analysis needing accurate calendar conversions. The backend algorithm normalizes inputs to UTC timestamps, computes deltas using epoch time, then converts results back to local time representations while preserving calendar consistency. Advanced features include Gregorian calendar validation, support for BC/AD notation, and precision down to the millisecond.
usage_steps: Select calculation mode using the toggle switch: 'Difference Between Dates' or 'Adjust Date by Duration'
Enter start date in format selector (YYYY-MM-DD, MM/DD/YYYY, or DD-MMM-YYYY) using the interactive calendar widget
Input end date or duration in designated fields, specifying time units (days/hours/minutes) via dropdown menus
Choose output timezone from 400+ IANA options to control result localization
Click 'Calculate' to execute operation with precision up to 15 decimal places for fractional days
Review results displayed in both absolute date format and relative duration notation
usage_examples: A project manager calculating exact man-days between sprint start and deadline dates across multiple time zones
A financial analyst determining compound interest accrual periods with daily calculations spanning leap years
An historian analyzing duration between Gregorian calendar reform dates in different European regions
A DevOps engineer scheduling maintenance windows that account for DST transitions in server locations
